results.title: Bessel polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the $n$-th classical Bessel polynomial $y_n$ is the polynomial with rational coefficients $y_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{(n+k)!}{2^k \, k! \, (n-k)!} \, x^k$.

results.title: Explicit formula for the Bessel polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Bessel polynomial $y_n \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ equals $\sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{(n+k)!}{2^k \, k! \, (n-k)!} \, x^k$.

results.title: A common prime divisor of $x - 1$ and $\Phi_p(x)$ is $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ and $p$ be primes, let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. If $\rho \mid x - 1$ and $\rho \mid \Phi_p(x)$, then $\rho = p$.

results.title: Divisibility of $x^p - 1$ by $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. Then $p \mid x^p - 1$ if and only if $p \mid x - 1$ and $p \mid \Phi_p(x)$.

results.title: Divisibility of $x^{rp^a} - 1$ by $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $r$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $r$ coprime to $p$, let $x$ be a positive integer, and let $\Phi_p$ be the $p$-th cyclotomic polynomial with integer coefficients. results.title: Liao–Li–Pu criterion for primitive element sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$ and $n$ be coprime natural numbers with $q^n > 2$, and let $\omega$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $q^n - 1$. results.title: Bunyakovsky condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ satisfies the Bunyakovsky condition when it has degree at least $1$, is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, and has positive leading coefficient.

results.title: Schinzel condition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $F$ of integer polynomials satisfies the Schinzel condition when it has no fixed prime divisor: for every prime $p$ there is a natural number $n$ such that $p$ divides none of the values $f(n)$ for $f \in F$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a complex normed space, and write $\hat g(y) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{-2\pi i x y} g(x)\,dx$ for the Fourier transform of a function $g : \mathbb{R} \to E$. results.title: Containment of a length-3 pattern
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence $e = e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ of natural numbers contains the length-3 pattern $p = p_0 p_1 p_2$ of natural numbers when there are positions $i_0 < i_1 < i_2$ in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ such that, for all $a, b \in \{0, 1, 2\}$, $e_{i_a} < e_{i_b}$ if and only if $p_a < p_b$; that is, the subsequence $e_{i_0} e_{i_1} e_{i_2}$ is order-isomorphic to $p$.

results.title: Short sequences contain no length-3 pattern
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Number of inversion sequences avoiding a set of patterns
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An inversion sequence of length $n$ is a sequence $e = e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ of natural numbers with $e_i \le i$ for every $i$. It contains a length-3 pattern $p = p_0 p_1 p_2$ (a triple of natural numbers) when some subsequence $e_a e_b e_c$ with $a < b < c$ is order-isomorphic to $p$. results.title: Linear threshold function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is a linear threshold function if there are reals $w_0, w_1, \dots, w_n$ such that for every $x \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ we have $f(x) = \operatorname{sgn}(w_0 + w_1 x_1 + \dots + w_n x_n)$, where $x_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ is the $i$-th coordinate of $x$, $\operatorname{sgn} z = 1$ for $z \ge 0$ and $\operatorname{sgn} z = -1$ for $z < 0$.

results.title: Majority function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the majority function $\mathrm{Maj}_n : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is given by $\mathrm{Maj}_n(x) = 1$ if $x_1 + \dots + x_n \ge 0$ and $\mathrm{Maj}_n(x) = -1$ otherwise, where $x_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ is the $i$-th coordinate of $x$.

results.title: Noise stability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $\rho$ and a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the noise stability of $f$ at $\rho$ is $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho[f] = \sum_{S \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}} \rho^{|S|} \hat f(S)^2$, where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.

results.title: Majority Is Least Stable conjecture in $n$ variables
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the statement that every linear threshold function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho[f] \ge \mathrm{Stab}_\rho[\mathrm{Maj}_n]$ for every real $\rho$ with $0 \le \rho \le 1$, where $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho$ is the noise stability and $\mathrm{Maj}_n$ is the majority function.

results.summary: For a cuckoo hash table $T$ with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ and a key $k$, the lookup of $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table holds a pair $(k, v)$; otherwise it returns $v$ if slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table holds a pair $(k, v)$; otherwise it returns nothing. No other slot is examined.

results.title: Lookup in the empty cuckoo hash table
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Looking up any key in the empty cuckoo hash table finds no value.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup finds a key in its first-table slot
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup finds a key in its second-table slot
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table of $T$ holds the pair $(k, v)$ and slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table of $T$ holds no pair whose key is $k$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.

results.title: Soundness of cuckoo lookup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$, then the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of the first or the second table of $T$.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup finds every stored key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant, and let $k$ be a key and $v$ a value. If the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of either table of $T$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns some value.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup finds every stored binding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. For every key $k$ and value $v$, if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in $T$, then looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup finds exactly the stored bindings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. For every key $k$ and value $v$, looking up $k$ in $T$ returns $v$ if and only if the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in $T$.

results.title: Slot holds a key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A slot of a cuckoo hash table is either empty or holds a pair $(k, v)$ of a key and a value. For a slot $s$ and a key $k'$, this test is true when $s$ holds a pair whose key is $k'$, and false when $s$ is empty or holds a pair with a different key.

results.title: Cuckoo hash insertion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$, with fuel $n$, either returns a table or fails. If slot $h_1(k)$ of the first table holds a binding for $k$, that slot is overwritten with $(k, v)$, and slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table is cleared if it also holds a binding for $k$, so no stale competing value remains. Otherwise, if slot $h_2(k)$ of the second table…

results.title: Cuckoo insertion stores the inserted binding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then the binding $k \mapsto v$ is stored in some slot of either table of $T'$.

results.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves the placement invariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant. If inserting the binding $k \mapsto v$ into $T$ (which replaces an existing binding for $k$ in place) with some fuel bound succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then $T'$ satisfies the placement invariant.

results.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves key determinism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table that satisfies the placement invariant and is key-deterministic. If inserting a key $k$ with value $v$ into $T$ with some fuel succeeds with result $T'$, then $T'$ is key-deterministic. In particular, replacement leaves no stale copy of $k$ with a different value in the other slot.

results.title: Cuckoo lookup returns an inserted value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant and stores each key with at most one value. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then looking up $k$ in $T'$ returns $v$.

results.title: Cuckoo insertion preserves the bindings of other keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant. Suppose inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$. Then for every key $k' \ne k$ and every value $v'$, the binding $k' \mapsto v'$ is stored in $T'$ if and only if it is stored in $T$.

results.title: Cuckoo insertion leaves lookups of other keys unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a cuckoo hash table with hash functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ that satisfies the placement invariant and stores each key with at most one value. If inserting (or replacing) the binding $k \mapsto v$ in $T$ with fuel $f$ succeeds and returns the table $T'$, then for every key $k' \ne k$, looking up $k'$ in $T'$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $T$: either both return nothing or both return the same…

results.title: Annotated commands
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An annotated command is built like an IMP command, from skip, assignments $x := a$ of an arithmetic expression $a$ to a variable $x$ (a natural number), sequential composition $C_1;\,C_2$ and conditionals $\mathrm{if}\ b\ \mathrm{then}\ C_1\ \mathrm{else}\ C_2$ on a boolean expression $b$, except that every while loop $\{I\}\ \mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ C$ also carries an assertion $I$, its invariant.

results.title: Erasing annotations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The IMP command $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ underlying an annotated command $C$ is obtained by deleting the invariant of every while loop: skip, assignments, sequential composition and conditionals are kept with their parts stripped, and $\{I\}\ \mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ C'$ becomes $\mathrm{while}\ b\ \mathrm{do}\ \mathrm{strip}(C')$.

results.title: Precondition of an annotated command
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$ (the postcondition), the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ is the assertion computed backwards as follows: $\mathrm{pre}(\mathrm{skip}, Q) = Q$; $\mathrm{pre}(x := a, Q)$ holds in a state $s$ iff $Q$ holds in the state obtained from $s$ by giving $x$ the value of $a$ in $s$; $\mathrm{pre}(C_1;\,C_2, Q) = \mathrm{pre}(C_1, \mathrm{pre}(C_2, Q))$; the precondition of…

results.title: Verification condition of an annotated command
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$ (the postcondition), the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ is the proposition defined as follows, where $\mathrm{pre}$ is the precondition of an annotated command: $\mathrm{vc}(\mathrm{skip}, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(x := a, Q)$ are true; $\mathrm{vc}(C_1;\,C_2, Q)$ holds iff $\mathrm{vc}(C_1, \mathrm{pre}(C_2, Q))$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C_2, Q)$ hold; the…

results.title: Soundness of verification conditions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an annotated command $C$ and an assertion $Q$, write $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ for the precondition and the verification condition of $C$ for the postcondition $Q$, and $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ for the IMP command obtained from $C$ by erasing its loop invariants. For every such $C$ and $Q$, if $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, then the Hoare triple $\{\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)\}\ \mathrm{strip}(C)\ \{Q\}$ is…

results.title: Verification conditions yield valid Hoare triples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be an annotated command, let $\mathrm{strip}(C)$ be the IMP command obtained from $C$ by erasing its loop invariants, and let $P$, $Q$ be assertions. If the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$, then the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\ \mathrm{strip}(C)\ \{Q\}$ is valid.

results.title: Weakening the postcondition of an annotated command
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be an annotated command and $Q$, $Q'$ assertions such that $Q$ entails $Q'$, and write $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ for the precondition and the verification condition of $C$ for the postcondition $Q$. If $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, then $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$ entails $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q')$ and $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q')$ holds.

results.title: Completeness of verification conditions for derivable triples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be an IMP command and $P$, $Q$ assertions such that the Hoare triple $\{P\}\ c\ \{Q\}$ is derivable in the partial-correctness Hoare logic. Then there is an annotated command $C$ such that erasing its loop invariants gives $c$, that is $\mathrm{strip}(C) = c$, the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$.

results.title: Completeness of verification conditions for valid triples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be an IMP command and $P$, $Q$ assertions such that the partial-correctness Hoare triple $\{P\}\ c\ \{Q\}$ is valid. Then there is an annotated command $C$ such that erasing its loop invariants gives $c$, that is $\mathrm{strip}(C) = c$, the verification condition $\mathrm{vc}(C, Q)$ holds, and $P$ entails the precondition $\mathrm{pre}(C, Q)$.
